# architecture.md ## Project Architecture Overview **hevy-mcp** is a [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server for the [Hevy](https://www.hevyapp.com/) fitness API. It lets AI assistants read, analyze, create, and update workouts, routines, exercise templates, and body measurements through authenticated Hevy API requests [[1]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/86385d8b-fd28-42af-bebd-e017cd533d92). The codebase is a TypeScript monorepo organized as a **private workspace orchestrator** with six packages under `packages/`. The root has no runtime `src/` tree — all implementation lives in the workspaces [[2]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6). The defining architectural property is that a **single MCP tool contract runs identically on two very different runtimes**: ```text Hosted: AI assistant → Streamable HTTP → Cloudflare Worker → Hevy API Local: AI assistant → MCP over stdio → local hevy-mcp → Hevy API ``` [[3]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/86385d8b-fd28-42af-bebd-e017cd533d92) This is achieved by keeping the tool implementations and API client runtime-neutral, then composing them into runtime-specific adapters (Node.js and Cloudflare Workers) that never share code with each other [[4]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae). The six workspaces and their roles at a glance: | Workspace | Package name | Role | | ---------------------- | ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | | `packages/hevy-client` | `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` | Runtime-neutral API client (Kubb-generated) | | `packages/operations` | `@hevy-mcp/operations` | Runtime-neutral shared operations layer | | `packages/core` | `@hevy-mcp/core` | Runtime-neutral MCP tools and server construction | | `packages/node` | `hevy-mcp` | Node.js stdio/HTTP adapter — the only publishable workspace | | `packages/worker` | `@hevy-mcp/worker` | Private Cloudflare Worker HTTP/OAuth adapter | | `packages/cli` | `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli` | Public Hevy command-line client | [[5]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6) ## Workspace Dependency Diagram The shipped composition graph flows from the runtime-neutral packages outward to the platform adapters and public CLI [[6]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae): ```mermaid graph TD HC["@hevy-mcp/hevy-client
runtime-neutral API client"] OPS["@hevy-mcp/operations
runtime-neutral operations layer"] CORE["@hevy-mcp/core
runtime-neutral MCP tools & server"] NODE["hevy-mcp
Node.js stdio/HTTP adapter"] WORKER["@hevy-mcp/worker
Cloudflare Worker HTTP/OAuth adapter"] CLI["@chrisdoc/hevy-cli
public CLI"] HC --> OPS HC --> CORE OPS --> CORE CORE --> NODE CORE --> WORKER CORE --> CLI style HC fill:#d4edda,stroke:#28a745 style OPS fill:#d4edda,stroke:#28a745 style CORE fill:#d4edda,stroke:#28a745 style NODE fill:#cce5ff,stroke:#004085 style WORKER fill:#fff3cd,stroke:#856404 style CLI fill:#cce5ff,stroke:#004085 ``` **Legend:** Green = runtime-neutral · Blue = Node.js adapter · Amber = Cloudflare adapter Key constraints to observe in this diagram [[7]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6): - `hevy-client`, `operations`, and `core` are **runtime-neutral**: they contain no Node.js built-ins and no Cloudflare-specific bindings, making them safe to import and execute in either runtime. - `hevy-mcp` (Node) and `@hevy-mcp/worker` (Cloudflare) both consume `core` but **must never import each other**. This boundary is enforced by the `package-boundaries` validation lane [[8]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/c4ac07dbe84a7e83ba88a5073f0a83ab34af5c86/repository/validation-lanes.json#L209-L227). - `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli` bundles the runtime-neutral packages directly and does **not** depend on either adapter. - `@hevy-mcp/core` depends on both `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` and `@hevy-mcp/operations` [[9]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/packages/core/package.json#L20-L24); `@hevy-mcp/operations` depends on `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` [[10]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/packages/operations/package.json#L16-L18). > [!IMPORTANT] > The adapter packages (`hevy-mcp` and `@hevy-mcp/worker`) must never import one another. Violating this constraint would pull Node-specific or Cloudflare-specific code into the wrong runtime bundle and cause hard failures at runtime. ## Runtime-Neutral vs. Platform Adapters ### What "runtime-neutral" means A package is **runtime-neutral** when it makes no assumptions about the JavaScript host environment. Concretely, this means: - **No Node.js built-ins**: `process`, `fs`, `child_process`, `path`, `crypto` (Node's version), etc. are forbidden. - **No Cloudflare-specific bindings**: KV namespaces, Durable Objects, environment secrets injected via `env` object, and Worker-specific globals are forbidden. - **Standard Web APIs only**: `fetch`, `URL`, `TextEncoder`, `crypto` (Web Crypto), and the rest of the [WinterCG](https://wintercg.org/) baseline. The two packages that must satisfy this constraint are `packages/hevy-client` and `packages/core` [[11]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae). The `packages/operations` layer also sits in this neutral zone — it depends only on `hevy-client` and adds no platform imports [[10]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/packages/operations/package.json#L16-L18). ### The adapter pattern Platform-specific concerns are isolated to the adapter packages: | Package | Owns | | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `packages/node` | stdio transport, local Streamable HTTP transport, process lifecycle (`SIGTERM`/`SIGINT`), Node telemetry (Sentry, OTLP), stdio observability, update checks | | `packages/worker` | Cloudflare Worker HTTP entrypoint, Streamable HTTP handler, OAuth 2.1 layer (KV-backed), Cloudflare bindings and environment types | [[12]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae) ### Enforcement The `package-boundaries` lane (blocking, runs on Node 24 and 26) uses dependency-cruiser to statically validate that the boundary rules hold across the entire workspace graph [[8]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/c4ac07dbe84a7e83ba88a5073f0a83ab34af5c86/repository/validation-lanes.json#L209-L227). ## 1. `packages/hevy-client`

### Public surface (must stay Promise-stable)

**Exports** (`/root/hevy-mcp/packages/hevy-client/package.json`):
- `.` → `/root/hevy-mcp/packages/hevy-client/src/index.ts`

**Public `HevyClient`** (`/root/hevy-mcp/packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client.ts`): all methods are **Promise-only**:

| Domain | Promise methods |
|---|---|
| Workouts | `getWorkouts`, `getWorkout`, `createWorkout`, `updateWorkout`, `getWorkoutCount`, `getWorkoutEvents` |
| Routines | `getRoutines`, `getRoutineById`, `createRoutine`, `updateRoutine` |
| Templates | `getExerciseTemplates`, `getExerciseTemplate`, `getExerciseHistory`, `createExerciseTemplate` |
| Folders | `getRoutineFolders`, `getRoutineFolder`, `createRoutineFolder` |
| Body measurements | `getBodyMeasurements`, `getBodyMeasurement`, `createBodyMeasurement`, `updateBodyMeasurement` |
| User | `getUserInfo` |

`createHevyClient` attaches `NATIVE_REQUEST_EFFECT` as a non-enumerable Symbol property — **not** part of the public type.

### Internal Effect seam

**File:** `/root/hevy-mcp/packages/hevy-client/src/internal-request-effect.ts`  
**Re-export:** `/root/hevy-mcp/packages/hevy-client/src/internal.ts`

| Name | Role |
|---|---|
| `NATIVE_REQUEST_EFFECT` | Private Symbol attachment |
| `NativeRequestEffect` | Low-level `RequestConfig → Effect.Effect<ResponseConfig<T>, unknown>` |
| `HevyRequestEffectClient` | Curated **Effect-backed reads only** |
| `getNativeRequestEffect(client)` | Retrieve interpreter |
| `getRequestEffectClient` / `createRequestEffect` | Build Effect read facade |

**Effect-backed methods on `HevyRequestEffectClient` (only 4):**
1. `getWorkouts`
2. `getWorkout`
3. `getRoutines`
4. `getRoutineById`

Everything else is **Promise-only** on public `HevyClient`. No Effect create/update/delete/events/count/templates/folders/body/user methods.

### Request interpreter (deep Effect usage)

**File:** `/root/hevy-mcp/packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client-kubb.ts`

- Builds `requestEffect` via `Effect.suspend` + `Effect.gen`
- Retry via `createRetrySchedule` + `Schedule.toStep` (`/root/hevy-mcp/packages/hevy-client/src/retry-schedule.ts`)

- Promise API is thin: `Effect.runPromise(createRequestEffect(config))`
- Imports: `Cause`, `Duration`, `Effect`, `Option`, `Schedule`, type-only `effect/Pull`

**File:** `/root/hevy-mcp/packages/hevy-client/src/effect-errors.ts`  
`Schema.TaggedError` classes: `RateLimitError`, `ValidationError`, `NotFoundError`, `NetworkError`, `ApiError`  
Re-exported from public `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` and re-exported by core (`/root/hevy-mcp/packages/core/src/effect-errors.ts`).

**Note:** Runtime path still primarily uses `HevyHttpError` (`/root/hevy-mcp/packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-http-error.ts`). Tagged Effect errors are foundation vocabulary; operations classify via pure `isHevyHttpError` helpers, not these tags yet.

- **No public `.effect()` method**

- Internally: Effect program → **one** `Effect.runPromise` boundary

- Body measurements  
- User info

## Concrete gaps / adoption frontiers

1. **Effect read coverage is 4 endpoints only** — no Effect methods for events, count, templates, folders, body, user, or any writes.
2. **Operations package is thin** — only workouts/routines list+get; soft-404 classification hard-coded to those two collections.
3. **Most MCP tools still call Promise client** — only 4 tools use `HevyOperationsService`; workflows and routine-discovery reimplement pagination instead of ops.
4. **No Effect program composition at tool layer** — tools are async handlers; services are lookup + Promise; no `Effect.gen` tool bodies.
5. **`Effect.fn` / Stream / Cache / DateTime unused** — caching is hand-rolled Promise TTL.
6. **Tagged Effect errors vs `HevyHttpError` dual vocabulary** — ops/tools still branch on HTTP error objects.
7. **Public ops API is Promise-only** — collapse is deliberate; no dual `effect`/`execute` surface yet.
8. **Adapters barely adopt Effect** — node/worker production code doesn’t run Effect programs; CLI uses ops Promise API.
9. **Docs gap** — architecture describes ops layer, not a phased Effect migration plan.
10. **`get-user-info` inconsistency** — uses `getClient()` rather than `HevyClientService` (and user tools not in main `hevyToolDefinitions` list).

## Mental model (current architecture)

```text
Public HevyClient (Promise)
        │
        ├─ NATIVE_REQUEST_EFFECT (Symbol, internal)
        │         │
        │         ▼
        │   requestEffect interpreter (Effect.gen + Schedule retry)
        │         │
        │         ▼
        │   HevyRequestEffectClient (4 GETs)  [@hevy-mcp/hevy-client/internal]
        │         │
        │         ▼
        │   operations.workouts|routines .{list,get}.execute → Promise
        │         │
        ▼         ▼
  HevyClientService   HevyOperationsService   (Context tags, request-local Layer)
        │         │
        └──── MCP tools (mostly Promise handlers) ────┘
```

**Bottom line:** Effect is **production-real** for the Hevy HTTP retry interpreter and for the four read operations’ internal programs, with request-local DI scaffolding in core. Adoption is **not** complete: public surfaces remain Promise, most domains/tools bypass operations, and higher-level Effect patterns (fn, Stream, Cache, DateTime, Effect-native tool handlers) are unused.
